entry.title: Little's Law: Understanding how much tour system can handle
entry.summary:
Introduction
Little's Law is a simple formula that connects the number of items in the system, arrival rate, and average time. Its used when you need to know how many items per time your system can handle. The formula is really simple: 𝐿 = 𝜆 𝑊 L is the average number of items λ is the entry rate W is the average time an items spends in the system In summary: quantity = rate × time. It gets 10 requests per second. Each request takes 2 seconds to be completed. So, in order to know how many requests are in the system at the same time, I apply the Little's Law formula: L = 10 * 2. Applying this formula helps you understand your system's capacity, including latency and throughput. With these insights, you can make better decisions about scaling, introducing queues, or setting timeouts.

entry.title: .NET Interview questions: Key concepts explained
entry.summary:
What's the difference between IQueryable, IEnumerable and List?
IQueryable represents a query that is not executed yet. It allows building the query step by step and is typically executed when iterated. IEnumerable represents a sequence of data that is already in memory (or will be pulled into memory). It supports iteration and can use lazy execution List is a concrete collection in memory that implements IEnumerable. It is fully materialized and allows modification (add, remove, etc). Singleton creates a single instance for the entire lifetime of the application. The same instance is shared across all requests (e.g., cache service). Scoped creates one instance per request.
